title: Binary Classification with Logistic Regression and Classification Report
description: Split the breast cancer dataset with stratify=y_clf, train a StandardScaler + LogisticRegression pipeline, and compute hard predictions, class-1 probabilities, and the classification report.

steps.description: Load the breast cancer dataset (`0 = malignant`, `1 = benign`) and split `(X_clf, y_clf)` into 75% train and 25% test using `stratify=y_clf` to preserve class proportions.

Fit a `Pipeline` of `StandardScaler()` and `LogisticRegression(max_iter=1000)` on `(Xc_train, yc_train)`, then compute both `y_pred = clf.predict(Xc_test)` and `y_prob = clf.predict_proba(Xc_test)[:, 1]`, and print `classification_report`.

Compare lines 13 and 14: `clf.predict(Xc_test)` returns hard `0/1` labels using threshold `0.5`, whereas `clf.predict_proba(Xc_test)[:, 1]` extracts column `1`, the continuous probability $P(y=1 \mid x)$.

steps.question: Why does line 14 slice `[:, 1]` from `clf.predict_proba(Xc_test)`?
steps.answer: `predict_proba` returns a 2-column array `[P(y=0|x), P(y=1|x)]` for each test sample, so `[:, 1]` selects the predicted probability of class 1 (`benign`).

steps.description: Line 14 computes `y_prob`, storing the predicted class-1 probability for each of the 143 test samples.
Line 15 prints the precision, recall, f1-score, and support for `malignant` (53) and `benign` (90), with overall accuracy `0.99`.
